value.body: A management consultant works on a client's business problem for a few weeks or months: entering a market, cutting costs, reorganising a team or planning a government programme. Employers include consulting firms, the advisory arms of accounting firms, and in-house strategy teams. A day usually involves research, data analysis, building slides and client meetings.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: MBA or IPM, or a strong undergraduate degree for analyst roles

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Excel, PowerPoint, survey and data tools

items.label: MBA enrolment
items.note: About 17% of all postgraduate enrolment; all modes

items.label: MBA graduates (out-turn)
items.note: Based on actual institutional responses; only a small share enter consulting

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Most freshers enter through campus placements at management institutes as associates or analysts. Undergraduates join as business analysts and move up, often after an MBA. Selection usually involves case interviews.

value.title: At a glance
items: Hours are often long and travel can be frequent.
Entry is competitive and concentrated in campus hiring.
Next roles: consultant, engagement manager, or a move to corporate strategy.

value.title: MBA enrolment (regular mode)
value.note: Regular mode only, so lower than the all-modes total. MBA is one route among several into consulting.
